To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brush border B-isoform of creatine kinase (CK) is functionally coupled to myosin in a contractile ring that is present in circumferential rings in the brush border of intestinal epithelial cells, but that CK-myosin coupling is not present in the interrootlet domain of the brush border.

the brush border B-isoform of creatine kinase, which is localized in the terminal web, provides a functional coupling to the myosins that are present in the circum-ferential ring and that this coupling provides a selective advantage to circumferential ring contractile activity.

the brush border B-ck isozyme of creatine kinase (B-CK) is localized distinctly in both the terminal web region and the brush border inter-rootlet domain, and that functional coupling between B-CK and myosin II is limited to the terminal web region, where it imparts a selective, energetically advantageous, coupling to the circumferentially oriented myosin II of the brush border circum-ferential ring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energetics and function of brush border myosin and creatine kinase, and with the functional coupling between these two proteins in the terminal web of intestinal epithelial cells.
